ops.title: meshtrust-dns-collision
ops.body:
**Decision**: `meshtrust/parse.go` `build()` keys peers by `normalizeHost(DNSName)` in a Go map. Two Tailscale peers normalizing to the same DNS name made the surviving address set depend on Go's randomized map iteration order — nondeterministic ACROSS PROCESSES on byte-identical `tailscale status` JSON, so two daemons could compute different `TrustedPeer` verdicts for the same peer set (reproduced 4096x in review).

**Fix chosen**: fail-closed by name. On a normalized-name collision, drop *both* colliding peers from that name — the name resolves to no addresses, same as an unmatched host target. This is order-independent: collect nodes into `nodes[name]`, and the moment a second distinct entry maps to an already-populated name, mark the name ambiguous; ambiguous names are deleted from `nodes` before matching against registry targets. Any single-name outcome no longer depends on which peer the (randomized) `st.Peer` map visits first or last.

**Why fail-closed over deterministic-pick (sorted/union)**: this is a trust boundary — meshtrust answers `TrustedPeer`/`TrustedOrigin` for a daemon deciding whether to honor a remote request. A DNS-name collision between two distinct Tailscale node keys is itself an anomaly (stale MagicDNS record, a spoofed/reused hostname, a registry bug) worth treating with suspicion rather than silently resolved by an arbitrary tie-break (lowest addr, first-sorted nodekey, etc. all still "pick one attacker-adjacent identity over another" if the collision were adversarial). Dropping the name entirely denies both rather than risk trusting an address that's ambiguously attributed. Deliberately scoped to the *name*, not the whole build (unlike the existing "any unparseable address fails the whole build" rule) — an ambiguous peer shouldn't be able to blind trust for the entire mesh, only for its own contested name.

**Test**: `TestBuildCollisionDeterministic` in `meshtrust/parse_test.go` — two peers with distinct nodekeys/addrs but the same normalized `DNSName`, registry target pointing at that name, `build()` called 4096x; asserts every run agrees the host resolves to zero addrs and neither peer's IP lands in `snap.peers`.

**Consumer note**: synckit is a tag-dependency for cc-runtime/cc-orchestrate (see task #19/#20) — this fix needs a new synckit patch tag before those repos can pick it up.
